newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka launches employee share plan.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka launches employee share plan.

text.p: Croatian Zagrebacka Banka said on Friday it had launched an employee share ownership plan (ESOP) to better motivate its staff by giving them a portion of the bank's expected capital gain.
"We estimate that each participant could gain 150 percent (on their investment) after three years when the cycle ends," member of the bank's board Davor Holjevac told reporters.
He said Zagrebacka sold its employees 19 million German marks worth of treasury shares, which represent 1.6 percent of its current shareholder capital.
Assuming it is not increased, the bank expects its staff to own up to four percent of the bank by 2000, he added.
Zagrebacka has 11.5 percent of its shares in the hands of small private investors, but not many of them work for the bank.
The scheme, devised and carried out in cooperation with Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), was said to be the first implemented in any central and eastern European country.

It attracted almost 3,600 eligible employees, who paid up to two months' salary for what is effectively a 20 percent stake in the total investment. The remaining 80 percent was financed by UBS through a loan, which has to be repaid in full in three years.
Employees will have voting rights but no dividend -- this money will be used by the bank to pay the interest, officials said.
An ESOP company has been set up to act in case Zagrebacka's shares fall, jeopardising its employees' investment. It will compensate their initial stake and pay UBS should this happen.
"Not all companies in the west have such schemes," said UBS's Claudio Steffenoni. "It completely hedges the employees against any loss."
But it is unlikely that such a mechanism will have to be activated, he added.

Zagrebacka's shares have risen steadily since they were floated at home and abroad at some 500 kuna a year ago. They last traded at 2,035 kuna on Zagreb's bourse on Wednesday. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
